clue.text: Side bursts open when edges split, revealing bust

indicators.note: edges splitting off means the outermost letter at each end of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a bank is the side of a river
bursts open is ERUPTS, which loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seam gives way and something bursts open at the sides, as if a garment has split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like part of the burst garment picture, but it means broke, financially ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust is the informal way of saying a person or firm has become insolvent and failed.

clue.text: What may make one go and run into bar

indicators.note: one item is put into another, so it sits inside the second word

blocks.note: to bar is to prohibit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Something that sends a person off to run into a bar, like a pub crawl starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' here is the euphemism for a bowel movement: fibre helps you go.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal husk is dietary fibre, the classic remedy for constipation, so it helps a person to the toilet.

clue.text: Dodge work in search when leader goes

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and it goes away here
one word goes in the other, placed inside its letters

blocks.note: to search is to scout, losing its first letter
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Avoiding a job search after the boss leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasion of responsibility is a dodge, an excuse that lets someone avoid doing something.

clue.text: Group of stars breaking very large instruments

indicators.note: one thing breaking into another ends up sitting within its letters

blocks.note: OS is outsize, the clothing label for very large
Carina, the Keel, is a southern constellation

explanation.surface: A band of celebrities smashing enormous musical instruments on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' suggests a pop band; it is a constellation, Carina.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small egg-shaped wind instruments with finger holes, often of clay, so they are instruments.

clue.text: A dead loss in spring, having new £1 note in circulation

indicators.note: something in circulation goes round, so these letters wrap round the other word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a oner is slang for a one-pound note
to spring is to start, jump with surprise

explanation.surface: A pound note circulating in springtime turns out to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'in spring' sends the word for spring inside N plus ONER; a oner is British slang for a one-pound note or coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no chance of succeeding from the outset is a hopeless failure, a complete washout.

clue.text: Regret about most of one group of countries or another

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read from the end
most of a word is all but its final letter

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
OPEC, the oil-exporting countries, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Remorse over how one bloc of nations or another behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'another', meaning another group of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent, or the EU loosely, is a second group of countries besides the oil cartel.

clue.text: Bob maybe in musical party

blocks.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man called Bob appearing as a guest at a theatrical party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one style of haircut, so it is an example of a styled arrangement of a person's hair.

clue.text: Servant about to break large old pot

indicators.note: breaking into a word means lodging inside it

blocks.note: fat means large
C is circa, about
O is the abbreviation for old
a pot is a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A clumsy servant is about to break a big antique pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' suggests crockery; it is a belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, a general servant or handyman.

clue.text: Dithered, apparently unconcerned about netting fines

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards
netting something means catching it inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: someone deaf to a plea appears not to care
F is fine, the pencil grade, so FF is two of them

explanation.surface: Someone wavered, seemingly indifferent to the penalties being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: F for fine is the pencil-lead grade; to faff is British slang for to waste time fussing.
explanation.definitionFit: To faff about is to dither, fussing ineffectually without getting anything done.

clue.text: Picture of floor in frame of iron

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its border, its first and last letters
one item goes in another, sitting between its letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of iron
to floor is to knock out, KO

explanation.surface: A painting of a floor hung in an iron frame.
explanation.walkthrough: An ikon is a variant spelling of icon, a religious image.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional painting of a holy figure, so it is a picture.

clue.text: Might a bluestocking don it?

blocks.note: surface reading: an item of clothing an intellectual woman might put on
setter's reading: a scholarly woman, perhaps at a famous university, wearing footwear named after it

explanation.walkthrough: A bluestocking is a learned woman, and 'don' hints at a university don; the footwear is a laced shoe named after the university city.
explanation.definitionFit: A low laced leather shoe named after the English university city, the kind of sensible shoe a female academic might wear.

clue.text: Bronze bust initially appearing in newspaper articles

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word before it
appearing in something means showing up inside it

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid
first letter of bust
a and the are the two articles

explanation.surface: A bronze bust first features in a newspaper's articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bronze' and 'bust' suggest a sculpture; bronze is a verb, to tan.
explanation.definitionFit: To bronze is to tan the skin, which is what lying in the sun does.

clue.text: Filmmaker remade Crucible without core of actors

indicators.note: a remade film is made again differently, so the letters are rearranged
the core of a word is its centre, the middle letters
without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged word goes around

blocks.note: taken as written
the two middle letters of actors

explanation.surface: A director remakes Arthur Miller's play The Crucible without its central cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside: the shuffled play surrounds the middle of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernardo Bertolucci was the Italian director of The Last Emperor and Last Tango in Paris.

clue.text: More stingy about popping into local

indicators.note: popping into somewhere means going inside it

blocks.note: local means nearby
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tight-fisted about popping into the local pub for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like the pub; it is the adjective meaning nearby. Near is old-fashioned British for mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is a dated word for mean or tight-fisted, so its comparative means stingier.

clue.text: Pompous press briefly infiltrating regulars in Triads

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, with the last letter removed
regular letters are taken at even intervals, every other one
infiltrating means getting inside something

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of Triads
to press is to urge, cut short

explanation.surface: Journalists infiltrating Chinese criminal gangs and the regulars there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests journalists; it is the verb urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgid style is swollen and overblown, so it is pompous and bombastic in tone.

clue.text: Mostly frigid and unusually unbecoming

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: frigid without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being mostly cold and unusually unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra dig is short for the Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath one's dignity is unseemly, inappropriate to one's status or position.

clue.text: Fly from one place into another after a bit of cycling

indicators.note: cycling a little rotates the letters by one place, the last coming to the front

blocks.note: to set is to place
another word for place

explanation.surface: An insect flies from one spot to another after a short bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb; it is the insect. Moving the last letter of the doubled word to the front gives the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African bloodsucking insect that spreads sleeping sickness, a kind of fly.

clue.text: Bomber without escort over camp

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

blocks.note: unaccompanied
camp and gay are both used of flamboyant style

explanation.surface: A bomber flying without an escort over a military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'camp' a military base; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enola Gay was the B-29 aircraft that dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in 1945.

clue.text: Opens empty bottle and drinks?

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving just the outer letters

blocks.note: outside letters of bottle
gins are drinks

explanation.surface: Someone uncorks a bottle that is emptied, perhaps of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opens' suggests uncorking; it means starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To open is to start or commence something, as a speaker or a game does.

clue.text: Dismissal by female following sex

indicators.note: following means coming after, so these letters are placed after the earlier word

blocks.note: a lay is slang for sex
by, as in a work of an author
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman sacked after an affair at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A layoff is the discharge of workers from a job, usually for lack of work.

clue.text: Waylay old president after a minute

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so this name comes later in the word

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute
George Bush, a former US president

explanation.surface: Stopping an ex-president for a minute's chat.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush is to attack from hiding, so it means to lie in wait and waylay someone.

clue.text: Mark in English attained by slowcoach in French

indicators.note: one word is in another, sitting between its letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a scar is a mark
got means attained

explanation.surface: A grade in English won by a slow pupil studying French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' and 'English' suggest school grades, as does 'slowcoach in French'; the snail is the slowcoach and escargot is French for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a proverbially slow creature, and escargot is the French word for it.

clue.text: Stage production of Tintin?

blocks.note: split as tin and tin, and a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A theatre show based on Hergé's boy reporter Tintin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the comic hero's name as tin plus tin; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is the high-kicking dance performed on stage in Parisian cabarets, a stage production.

clue.text: Swearing in judge after old boy's given no time to start -- on the contrary

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so the letters follow the earlier ones
given no start means the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
J is the abbreviation for judge
duration is time, losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A judge is sworn in after an old boy is refused time to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'given no time to start' to time given no start.
explanation.definitionFit: Objuration is an archaic word for the act of binding by oath, as when someone is sworn into office.

clue.text: All the best food is picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so this is about how a word sounds

blocks.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Wishing everyone well as the food is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow is informal for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word is a casual farewell, a way to sign off wishing someone well.

clue.text: Cook using ceramic hob, eschewing fire at first

indicators.note: at first points at the opening letter of each of the words before

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A cook working on a ceramic hob and avoiding a naked flame.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is all decoy: the four words give their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who prepares food in a restaurant kitchen is a cook.

clue.text: We predict books will be ditched by those with mental health issues

definitions.note: a statement made by the plural noun about itself

indicators.note: ditched means thrown away, so those letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: people with psychosis
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A forecast that patients will throw away their reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We predict' is the answer speaking about itself, as fortune-tellers would.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyants claim to foresee the future, so as a group they could say they foretell events.

clue.text: On reflection, designate old man as missing link?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the words run backwards

blocks.note: to designate is to name
pa is father, the old man

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, naming one's father as the absent relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the missing link was the supposed ape-human intermediate.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed missing link between apes and humans was imagined as a primitive half-ape hominid.
